I recommend making a backup first (safer — avoids accidental data loss). If that sounds good, I can create a timestamped backup in the same directory and then overwrite /tmp/test.txt.

  - Backup: cp --preserve=mode,ownership,timestamps /tmp/test.txt /tmp/test.txt.bak
  - Overwrite: echo "new content" > /tmp/test.txt

- Create a timestamped backup (safer if you make multiple changes):
  - Backup: cp --preserve=mode,ownership,timestamps /tmp/test.txt /tmp/test.txt.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S).bak
  - Overwrite: echo "new content" > /tmp/test.txt

- If you need to preserve everything exactly (including SELinux context), consider using cp -a (or cp -p on macOS):
  - Backup: cp -a /tmp/test.txt /tmp/test.txt.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S).bak
